source: Voita and Titov (2020) Information-Theoretic Probing with Minimum Description Length
finding: Probe quality scored as description length of labels (online and variational codes) instead of accuracy. Random-label control tasks need much longer codes than real tasks, so MDL separates real structure from memorisation without a separate control-task correction.
numbers: POS tagging, ELMo layers. Layer 1 online code 115 kbits on the real task vs 717 kbits on the control task; layer 0 96 vs 515 kbits. Variational and online codes agree on ranking.
limits: One task family (POS, then others in the paper); code length mixes model cost and data cost.
agent_relevance: Evidence that a compression score can reject a fit that just memorises. Supports S7 using description length, not raw fit, as the tie-break.

source: Voita and Titov (2020) Information-Theoretic Probing with Minimum Description Length
finding: Accuracy ranks are unstable under probe settings and random seed; MDL ranks are stable.
numbers: Seed 1: layer 1 vs 2 accuracy 97.48 vs 97.31; seed 0: 97.38 vs 97.48 (order flips). Across 10 hyperparameter settings accuracy of linguistic vs control task flips sign for layer 0; MDL did not.
limits: Stability shown on probes of one architecture family (MLP); five seeds only.
agent_relevance: A tie-break between candidates should not flip with noise. Description length was less noisy than fit in this study.

source: Voita and Titov (2020) Information-Theoretic Probing with Minimum Description Length
finding: Probes trained on real labels prune to a small network; probes trained on random labels stay large. The variational code shows complexity differs, not only fit.
numbers: Pruned probe widths for the real task 33-75 neurons in later layers vs about 260-480 for the control task (Table 3). Compression ratios 31x vs 19x (variational) for the MLP-2 probe.
limits: Pruning method (Bayesian compression, Louizos 2017) is one choice among several.
agent_relevance: Shows the hypothesis-cost term does real work: real structure needs a short hypothesis, memorisation needs a long one.

source: Blier and Ollivier (2018) The description length of deep learning models
finding: Prequential (online) coding gives far tighter bounds than two-part float32 codes or variational codes for deep nets. A trained net's weights as a plain 2-part code cost more bits than the raw labels; the prequential code compresses.
numbers: MNIST uniform code 199 kbits; float32 2-part >8.6 Mbits (over 45x worse than uniform); variational >400 kbits; prequential 22.2 kbits (ratio 0.11); best compressed variant 4.10 kbits at 99.5% test acc. CIFAR10: uniform 166 kbits, prequential 89.0 kbits (0.54).
limits: Variational code was weak here; Voita and Titov (b01) found the variational code competitive on NLP probes, so the gap is not universal.
agent_relevance: Choice of code matters more than the principle. For a thinking scaffold, prefer a prequential-style score (how well the hypothesis predicts held-out items in order) over counting its own parameters.

source: Blier and Ollivier (2018) The description length of deep learning models
finding: Models that generalise well compress well even when heavily overparameterised; fake-label nets cannot compress.
numbers: MNIST with fake labels: codelength stays near the uniform code log2(10) bits per sample; true labels go far below.
limits: MNIST and CIFAR10 only.
agent_relevance: Supports G3: a fit with no compression gain is memorisation, not rule discovery.

source: Grunwald and Roos (2019) Minimum Description Length Revisited
finding: The standard overview. Modern MDL uses luckiness functions instead of priors and treats AIC vs BIC vs cross-validation as different code-length choices. Three updates since 2007: wider estimator classes, known sub-optimal behaviour under misspecification, and links to deep-learning generalisation (PAC-MDL bounds).
numbers: Not a numeric study. Gives the MDL/BIC expansion: code length = -log likelihood + (k/2) log n + O(1) for regular models.
limits: Theory review; most results asymptotic.
agent_relevance: Right frame for S7: the score is a code length with a stated luckiness choice, not a free-floating simplicity feeling.

source: Grunwald and Roos (2019) Minimum Description Length Revisited
finding: MDL and Bayes, unmodified, can behave sub-optimally or become inconsistent when all candidate models are wrong but some are useful. This is the main known failure mode. The Safe Bayesian fix tunes a learning rate.
numbers: Safe Bayesian algorithm introduced to repair misspecification inconsistency (Section 6.3); no single effect size.
limits: Fix is developed for specific model classes.
agent_relevance: Real tasks give no true model. A compression tie-break is least reliable when the agent's hypothesis class is wrong. Do not treat the shortest hypothesis as proven.

source: Grunwald and van Ommen (2017) Inconsistency of Bayesian Inference for Misspecified Linear Models, and a Proposal for Repairing It
finding: Bayes factor model selection, model averaging and Bayes ridge regression are inconsistent under misspecification: with heteroskedastic data and a homoskedastic model, the posterior piles onto ever-higher-dimensional models as n grows. SafeBayes (tempered likelihood, learning rate learned from data) selects small learning rates and repairs it.
numbers: Nested linear models M0..Mpmax; squared-error risk of the full Bayes predictor stays above SafeBayes as n grows (Figure 2).
limits: Simulation on a designed counterexample; SafeBayes is conservative.
agent_relevance: A direct failure case for naive MDL/Bayes: more data does not rescue a misspecified class. Keep the G3 held-out check as a guard.

source: Deletang et al. (2024) Language Modeling Is Compression
finding: Pretrained text LLMs used with arithmetic coding are strong general lossless compressors on images and audio, beating domain compressors.
numbers: Chinchilla 70B: ImageNet patches 43.4% of raw size vs PNG 58.5%; LibriSpeech 16.4% vs FLAC 30.3%; enwik9 8.3% (Llama 2 7B 8.9%). Random data stays near 100%.
limits: Raw rate ignores model size.
agent_relevance: Prediction and compression are the same object; a model's log-loss on a candidate is a legitimate description length of that candidate.

source: Deletang et al. (2024) Language Modeling Is Compression
finding: Two-part correction removes the headline: once parameter bytes are counted, big LMs lose to gzip and LZMA unless the data is terabytes.
numbers: Adjusted rate (model size added) for Chinchilla 70B is on the order of 1400-1500% of raw on 1 GB datasets (table garbled in text extraction, read approximately); gzip 32.3% on enwik9.
limits: Adjusted rate needs TB-scale data for LLMs to win; this is about total code length, not accuracy.
agent_relevance: The hypothesis-cost term is exactly what a scaffold must count. A very large hypothesis needs a lot of data to pay for itself, so short rule candidates win on small tasks.

source: Deletang et al. (2024) Language Modeling Is Compression
finding: Optimal model size depends on dataset size under the adjusted (two-part) rate: bigger models help on large data and hurt on small data.
numbers: Vanilla Transformers on enwik7/8/9: a critical size exists after which the adjusted rate rises again as parameters outweigh data.
limits: Small Transformers, enwik data only.
agent_relevance: Direct statement of the MDL trade-off for LMs. On a 3-example ARC item the cost term dominates.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Compression Represents Intelligence Linearly
finding: Across base LLMs, average benchmark score is near-linearly related to compression (bits per character) on fresh domain corpora.
numbers: 31 public LLMs, 12 benchmarks, three domains (knowledge and commonsense, coding, math). Pearson correlation about -0.95 per domain.
quote: Pearson correlation coefficient of around -0.95 for each evaluated domain of intelligence
limits: Base models only; short to medium context; may not hold for abilities not yet emerged; benchmark-overfit models appear as outliers; accuracy saturates near 0.8 on some tasks.
agent_relevance: Compression as an unsupervised model-quality signal. It ranks models, not single answers, so it does not by itself justify picking one candidate answer by code length.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Compression Represents Intelligence Linearly
finding: The authors' limitation list is evidence too: the link needs well-trained base models and does not cover fine-tuned chat models.
numbers: Fine-tuned models are not general-purpose compressors; long-context regime untested.
limits: Same study. No independent replication of the exact -0.95 found this session.
agent_relevance: Do not assume instruction-tuned agent outputs obey the compression-quality relation.

source: Yuan, Shao, Li (2025) Information Capacity: Evaluating the Efficiency of LLMs via Text Compression
finding: Follow-up on 56 open models: information capacity (compression relative to compute, with tokenizer efficiency) is stable within a model series and relates to benchmark scores across sizes.
numbers: 56 open-source models, five datasets; consistent capacity within a series; strong linguistic bias reported (compression differs by language).
limits: Authors' own metric; correlation values were not extracted from the figures here.
agent_relevance: Mild independent support for b12 with a different metric. Language bias warns that code length depends on the reference model.

source: Mazor, Morgan, Pass (2026) Language Modeling is Monotone Compression
finding: Theory: next-token predictors are equivalent to monotone (order-preserving) compressors, up to an additive gap of 2; monotonicity is needed exactly when cryptographic one-way functions exist.
numbers: Equivalence gap of 2 (in error); no empirical numbers.
limits: Pure theory; says nothing about reasoning quality.
agent_relevance: Formal basis for treating LM log-loss as code length, but not evidence that shorter code means better reasoning.

source: Elmoznino et al. (2025) In-Context Learning and Occam's Razor
finding: Next-token loss over a context equals prequential code length, so training an in-context learner minimises training error plus the complexity of the implicitly learned model. In-context learners generalised better than SGD learners in the low-data regimes tested.
numbers: Tasks include Mastermind and linear regression; ICL trained on the full sequence generalises better than ICL trained on only the later half (which loses the low-data signal).
limits: Controlled synthetic tasks.
agent_relevance: Same logic as b04: the early examples' cost is what penalises complex hypotheses. Example order matters for a prequential score.

source: Elmoznino et al. (2025) In-Context Learning and Occam's Razor
finding: Failure case: a large pretrained LLM does not minimise prequential code length on a novel task.
numbers: GPT-4 had much higher cross-entropy than small ICL models trained on Mastermind tasks and than a naive baseline predicting the marginal label distribution (5 seeds; exact values only in the figure).
limits: Single novel task; GPT-4 only.
agent_relevance: Do not assume a frontier model's in-context behaviour is Occam-optimal on a novel rule. The scaffold must supply the code-length check.

source: Elmoznino et al. (2025) In-Context Learning and Occam's Razor
finding: The ICL-compression match depends on architecture: SGD-based learners did as well in some settings and better in large-data regimes on Mastermind.
numbers: SGD matched or beat ICL on Mastermind at large data sizes.
limits: Small models, synthetic tasks.
agent_relevance: The compression link is not a free win for the Transformer; boundary condition on use.

source: Abudy et al. (2025) A Minimum Description Length Approach to Regularization in Neural Networks
finding: Standard L1, L2 or no regularisation push networks away from perfect hand-built solutions on formal languages; MDL regularisation keeps the perfect solution as the optimum.
numbers: Tasks anbn, anbncn, Dyck-1, Dyck-2, arithmetic, toy English. Dyck-1: MDL net |H|=139, test gap +0.1% vs golden; L1/L2 nets are 460-600 units for some tasks with test gaps up to 11.4-13.0% (table in paper).
limits: Needs a hand-built golden network for reference; gradient descent cannot optimise the MDL objective, so search uses a genetic algorithm.
agent_relevance: Strong case for scoring hypotheses by total code length rather than fit plus an ad hoc penalty. Search is the open cost.

source: Shaw et al. (2026) Bridging Kolmogorov Complexity and Deep Learning: Asymptotically Optimal Description Length Objectives for Transformers
finding: Proves asymptotically optimal description length objectives exist for Transformers and builds a differentiable variational one. The objective selects low-complexity, generalising solutions, but standard optimisers cannot find them from random init.
numbers: Identity-task MLP: random-init variational run did not reach the loss of a hand-built solution; hand init gave 100% accuracy at about 3.4e2 bits, while KL coef 1.0 gave 54% accuracy at 2.64e3 bits. Only the manually initialised Transformer showed strong length generalisation.
limits: Small algorithmic tasks; the optimisation failure is the key limit.
agent_relevance: Same lesson as b19 from a second lab: MDL picks the right answer, but search to reach it is the bottleneck. A scaffold with explicit candidates avoids that problem.

source: Ferre (2025) MADIL: An MDL-based Framework for Efficient Program Synthesis in the ARC Benchmark
finding: A pure MDL program learner on ARC: MCTS over task models with value from compression. It generalises well when it finds a fit but covers few tasks.
numbers: 400 public evaluation tasks: 69 fit all training examples, 57 correct on test (generalisation 82%); 53 of 57 correct on first attempt; abstract reports 7% at ArcPrize 2024, below LLM methods; 80% of solutions found in the first 20 s.
limits: Low recall; DSL limits coverage.
agent_relevance: Fit-then-compress picked generalising programs 82% of the time, supporting an S7 tie-break only among candidates that already fit. It does not replace candidate generation.

source: Nair and Wang (2024) MIDGARD: Self-Consistency Using Minimum Description Length for Structured Commonsense Reasoning
finding: MDL-based aggregation of sampled reasoning graphs from an LLM, rejecting rare properties and adding missing ones. Gains are clear on some tasks and near zero on others.
numbers: Semantic graph generation, gpt-3.5-turbo, T-F1: KELM 47.4 vs greedy 46.9; WebNLG 29.3 vs 29.1; GenWiki 24.3 vs 23.7. Code-Llama: KELM 37.9 vs 37.9, WebNLG 26.5 vs 24.8. Argument-graph essays, bin [20,25): C 75.5 vs 65.7 greedy.
limits: Changes are small on semantic graph tasks; hyperparameters estimated per task; samples from one model are correlated (G4).
agent_relevance: Closest LLM use of MDL as an aggregator. Gains are modest and structure-dependent; evidence for G5 (code selects), not for a large benefit.

source: Gao et al. (2026) RIMRULE: Improving Tool-Using Language Agents via MDL-Guided Rule Learning
finding: An LLM proposes rules from failure traces; MDL consolidation keeps rules short and general. Consolidation lowers rule count while holding or raising accuracy.
numbers: Initial 72 rules (ToolHop) and 151 (BFCL); consolidation cut rule count 7% and 20% with accuracy gains on test-rand and smaller gains on test-unseen. Low-data case: 90 training samples, four rules, accuracy 55.2% to 62.1% (test-rand) and 46.0% to 60.0% (test-unseen), BFCL multi_turn_base.
limits: Consolidation gain not separated from rule injection in the numbers read; the objective is partly LLM-judged.
agent_relevance: Matches G2 (learn from real failing output) and S7. An MDL pruning step did not hurt and shortened the prompt.

source: Ganeshan (2026) Where Induction Runs Out: Description-Length Difficulty and the Memorisation Gap in Integer-Sequence Benchmarks
finding: An exact two-part MDL learner over P-recursive recurrences gives a contamination-free difficulty score. The discovery point n_d (first prefix where a rule beats verbatim storage) depends on hypothesis size, not term magnitude.
numbers: n_d matches the identifiability bound exactly in 89% of cases; correlation with growth r=-0.007; with structural size r=+0.85. Of 20,000 OEIS sequences, 89.98% that fit a recurrence on some prefix fit none at full length. Abstention on no-theory sequences: Claude Sonnet 4.5 64.7%, GPT-4o 95.0%, Llama 3.3 70B 89.5%.
limits: Single preprint by an independent researcher, not peer reviewed; LLM samples of 17-20 per stratum.
agent_relevance: A concrete rule: compare literal storage cost with rule cost to decide when a rule is justified. Confident errors on easy items suggest memorisation, so recognised patterns still need a held-out check.

source: Deletang et al. (2024) Language Modeling Is Compression
finding: Compression ability transfers across modalities: text-only Chinchilla compresses images and audio it was not trained on, so the gain is in-context learning.
numbers: Raw enwik9 rates for Chinchilla 1B/7B/70B: 11.3/10.2/8.3%.
limits: Raw rates; adjusted rates cancel the advantage.
agent_relevance: Evidence that an LM's likelihood already contains in-context rule learning.

source: Rissanen (1978) Modeling by shortest data description
finding: The founding paper: choose the model giving the shortest code for model plus data; leads to the (k/2) log n penalty.
numbers: Not opened this session.
limits: Background only.
agent_relevance: Cite as origin; rely on b06 for the modern form.

source: Schwarz (1978) Estimating the dimension of a model
finding: Independent Bayesian derivation of the same (k/2) log n penalty (BIC); MDL and BIC agree asymptotically for regular models.
numbers: Not opened; relation stated in b06.
limits: Background only.
agent_relevance: Same penalty from two routes.

source: Hewitt and Liang (2019) Designing and Interpreting Probes with Control Tasks
finding: Control tasks and selectivity were the earlier fix for probes that memorise; Voita and Titov (b01-b03) argue description length handles this without tuning probe size.
numbers: Not opened; description taken from b01 text.
limits: Second-hand.
agent_relevance: Prior rival method to MDL probing.
